reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.118.1-Ps.118.4 re-derived from bytes. Psalm 118 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map rule 'identity'), so web and MT numbering coincide 1:1 and no dual-cite arithmetic is owed; all 3 oshb: citations in the row resolve to their own verses. All 3 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against their cited refs (collate.py: 3/3 byte). Refrain claim re-derived independently rather than trusted: the 3-token clause כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ sliced from oshb:Ps.118.2 is a byte substring of oshb:Ps.118.1, 118.2, 118.3 and 118.4 -- 4 verses -- and of no further verse in the psalm except oshb:Ps.118.29 (1 verse), so the row's span-scoped count is exact. Inclusio claim re-derived: oshb:Ps.118.1 and oshb:Ps.118.29 are byte-equal as WHOLE verses, 7 whitespace tokens each (the staged extract is maqaf-free, so the kî-tôb pair counts as 2 tokens), and verse-initial hodu falls at exactly 2 verses in this psalm, oshb:Ps.118.1 and oshb:Ps.118.29 -- matching the device inventory's hodu frame; the psalm's own frame is therefore stronger than the row needs. The Ps 115 roster mirrors member for member and Ps 115 is likewise identity-numbered: “Israel, trust in Yahweh!” (web:Ps.115.9), “House of Aaron, trust in Yahweh!” (web:Ps.115.10), “You who fear Yahweh, trust in Yahweh!” (web:Ps.115.11), all 3 mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs, and the row correctly reports the jussive 'let...say' displacing the imperative rather than claiming formal identity. Disclosure obligations: pmarks_Ps.json carries 0 selah verses and 0 ketiv/qere notes across this psalm's 29 verses, and the book carries no pe/samekh layer (book-wide: 0 segs), so nothing is owed and nothing is claimed. One observation, not a defect: the gloss “for his loving kindness endures forever” is WEB's wording at web:Ps.118.1, while the Hebrew beside it is cited from oshb:Ps.118.2, where WEB instead reads “that his loving kindness endures forever” (web:Ps.118.2); the Hebrew is byte-identical across those 2 verses, so the argument is unaffected.

Span Ps.118.5-Ps.118.9 verified. All 9 Hebrew runs in this row collate at byte tier against their cited refs (collate.py batch: 9/9 byte, including the two wordplay tokens and both proverb openings). The doubled-proverb claim re-derived from bytes rather than trusted: oshb:Ps.118.8 and oshb:Ps.118.9 are 5 whitespace tokens each and share their first 4 tokens byte-for-byte, diverging only at the final token, so 'diverging solely at the final word' is exact -- and, if anything, understated, since the shared run extends one token past the quoted opening clause. The seam at 118:4|118:5 is a genuine tier-1 voice shift: the triadic communal call gives way to first-person report, “Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.” (web:Ps.118.5), and the seam at 118:9|118:10 opens the battle report. The distress/space pair is a semantic antithesis across two roots rather than paronomasia in the strict sense, but the row claims a 'wordplay' between the 2 byte-true tokens and both are byte-confirmed in oshb:Ps.118.5, so the claim carries. Count objects are named with units (2 verses, 1 verse) and each carries a digit. No selah, ketiv/qere, paseq, inverted-nun or suspended-letter object falls in 118:5-9 (pmarks_Ps.json), so no disclosure is owed. The WEB fragment attributed to web:Ps.118.6-7 is drawn wholly from v6, but v6-7 is the declaration the row describes and the fragment is verbatim inside it (1 verse of the 2 cited), so this is citation breadth, not a misquote.

Span Ps.118.10-Ps.118.14 is well placed and I do not contest it: the tripled surrounding report and its adversative resolution hold together, the 118:9|118:10 and 118:14|118:15 seams are both tier-1 voice/scene shifts, and confidence 'medium' is honestly calibrated for a row whose internal 10-12|13-14 seam is a live rival. All 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against their cited refs, and the psalm's identity numbering means no dual-cite is owed. Two of the row's evidence claims fail on re-derivation, however. First, the closing clause the row calls identical across the 3 verses IS byte-shared, but the row quotes 3 of its 4 tokens while glossing all 4. Second, and materially worse, the signal that carries the surround-verb argument quotes the refrain clause where it means the verb, so the 'long form' it names is not the form it shows; the underlying 4-occurrence count and the long/short distribution across 118:10-12 are correct nonetheless when re-derived from bytes, so the repair is a re-splice. A third, minor point: the 2 tokens of the short form are equal only at accent_stripped tier, and the row asserts sharing without naming that tier.

challenges.claim: The observed_substrate_signals entry that carries the surround-verb argument quotes the WRONG Hebrew for its 'long form': the string it labels the long spelling of the surround-verb is the row's own refrain clause, which does not contain that verb.
challenges.evidence: The row's long-form quote is בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם (oshb:Ps.118.10) -- the clause of 4 tokens the same row elsewhere calls the verses' identical closing clause. The surround-verb long spelling is 1 token, סְבָב֑וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.10), repeated byte-identically at סְבָב֑וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.11); both collate at byte tier. The verb's consonantal skeleton is not a substring of the skeleton of the quoted clause (containment test on ps_lib.skeleton output: false), so the quote cannot be the form it is said to be. Re-derived independently, the surround-verb occurs 4 times in oshb:Ps.118.10-118.12 -- long at 118:10 token 3 and 118:11 token 3, short (סַבּ֥וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.11), סַבּ֤וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.12)) at 118:11 token 1 and 118:12 token 1 -- so the row's structural description is right and only its quote is wrong; the fix is a re-splice, not a new argument.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync in the rationale: the Hebrew quoted for the tripled closing clause is 3 tokens while the gloss beside it renders 4, adding 'in ... name' with no Hebrew behind it.
challenges.evidence: The rationale quotes יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם (oshb:Ps.118.10) and glosses it “in Yahweh's name I cut them off” (web:Ps.118.10). The byte-identical closing clause shared by all 3 verses is one token longer: בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם (oshb:Ps.118.10), a byte substring of oshb:Ps.118.11 and oshb:Ps.118.12 (both confirmed). The quoted 3-token run is also byte-shared by the 3 verses, so the count survives, but the gloss covers a span the quote does not -- the quote must be re-cut to the 4-token clause (which is what the row's own 'identical clause' claim describes).

challenges.claim: Untiered identity claim: the short surround-verb form is said to be 'shared by' the opening token of 118:11 and 118:12, but the 2 tokens are not byte-identical.
challenges.evidence: Compared as 2 tokens, סַבּ֥וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.11) and סַבּ֤וּנִי (oshb:Ps.118.12) differ in their cantillation and are equal only after ps_lib.strip_accents (accent_stripped tier; byte tier false). The row names the tier for its other identity claims; this one needs the same treatment under the campaign's tier/ordinal discipline.

reviews.reasoning: The span Ps.118.15-Ps.118.18 stands and its central byte claim verifies: the last 4 tokens of oshb:Ps.118.15 are byte-identical to the tail of oshb:Ps.118.16, and all 3 Hebrew runs in the row collate at byte tier. The move from acclamation to first-person survival testimony at 118:16|118:17 is a real voice shift, and 'medium' confidence is right given the live 15-16|17-18 rival the row names. What fails is the row's account of the witness: WEB's embedded quotation does not begin where the row says it begins, and the Hebrew quoted as the quotation's opening is not the material WEB marks. Because the row's device_notes lean on the acclamation being 'quoted communal speech', getting the quotation's extent right matters. Observation, not a defect: pmarks_Ps.json records 1 paseq seg at MT Ps.118.15 (seg layer, single-witness); the staged verse bytes exclude it, so the row's byte-tier splice across that point is legitimate and the row correctly makes no mark claim.

challenges.claim: The row mislocates the quotation WEB actually marks in 118:15-16: it binds the Hebrew for 'the voice of rejoicing' to an opening quotation mark that WEB places later in the verse, before the right-hand clause.
challenges.evidence: In web:Ps.118.15 the U+201C sits at character index 71, after the words “The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous.” (web:Ps.118.15) and immediately before “The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly.” (web:Ps.118.15); the matching U+201D closes at the end of “The right hand of Yahweh is exalted! The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly!” (web:Ps.118.16). Those are the 2 verses in Ps 118 carrying quotation marks (swept over the WEB text of all 29 verses). So the marked quotation corresponds to יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (oshb:Ps.118.15) -- the very clause the row separately shows is doubled at oshb:Ps.118.16 (byte tier, tail-equality confirmed) -- not to ק֤וֹל רִנָּ֬ה (oshb:Ps.118.15). The seam and the doubling survive; the rendering claim and the quote bound to it do not.

reviews.reasoning: The gate seam is real and I support the span's edges: 118:18|118:19 is a scene and voice break (imperative plea to gatekeepers after first-person survival testimony) and 118:21|118:22 turns from address to interpretive saying. All 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier, including the meteg-bearing opening of oshb:Ps.118.20, which I checked because a meteg difference would have dropped it to accent_stripped. The gate count re-derived independently: a consonantal sweep of the gate noun over Ps 118 returns exactly 2 verses, 118:19 and 118:20, both inside the row, so that signal is exact. The psalm is identity-numbered, so no dual-cite is owed. My challenge is narrow and does not touch the span: the row's no-parallel claim about the voice pattern is both unswept and refuted by the psalm's own 118:25-118:28, where the same plea/reply/first-person sequence recurs with a byte-level lexical tie. I also record the mechanical refs-mirror gap. One further wording observation, below challenge threshold: the signal describes two voice shifts as occurring 'within 2 verses' while the shifts it lists run across 3 verses, 118:19 to 118:21.

challenges.claim: The row asserts that the plea/reply/testimony voice pattern lacks a parallel elsewhere in this part; that assertion is unswept and is falsified inside this same psalm (skeleton sweep of the tying verb form over Ps 118: 2 verses).
challenges.evidence: The same three-step sequence recurs at 118:25-118:28: an imperative plea addressed to the deity, אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה נָּ֑א (oshb:Ps.118.25), “Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh!” (web:Ps.118.25); a third-person declarative reply, בָּר֣וּךְ הַ֭בָּא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.118.26), “Blessed is he who comes in Yahweh's name!” (web:Ps.118.26); and resumed first-person address, אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ (oshb:Ps.118.28). The lexical tie is byte-level, not merely notional: the thanksgiving verb with 2ms suffix whose skeleton appears at oshb:Ps.118.21 (א֭וֹדְךָ) recurs at oshb:Ps.118.28 (וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ) -- a skeleton sweep of that form over Ps 118 returns exactly 2 verses, 118:21 and 118:28. The claim also passes check_universals only incidentally: the digit-bearing '2 verses' earlier in the same signal falls inside the checker's 160-character window, so the no-parallel assertion itself is never swept.

challenges.claim: Refs-mirror gap: verses argued in prose outside the row's span are not carried in boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.evidence: The rejected_alternative argues against the plea having an addressee inside vv14-18; resolved against the row's psalm that is Ps.118.14 through Ps.118.18, of which only web:Ps.118.18 appears in boundary_evidence_refs. check_refs_mirror.py flags Ps.118.14, Ps.118.15, Ps.118.16, Ps.118.17 as argued_but_unmirrored (4 verses).

reviews.reasoning: I do not contest the span itself -- Ps.118.22-Ps.118.24 is a defensible unit, the 118:21|118:22 turn from address to saying is real, and 'medium' confidence is appropriate. All 3 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against their cited refs and the psalm is identity-numbered, so no dual-cite is owed. But the warrant the row gives for the unit does not survive re-derivation: the 'this'-demonstrative triad it names is present in only 1 of the 3 verses in Hebrew and 2 of 3 in English, and the verse-initial demonstrative in this psalm falls at 118:20 and 118:24 -- that is, it crosses the seam the row opens rather than binding the row together, which under cross-seam cohesion argues against the row unless disclosed. The signal compounds this by quoting a prepositional phrase and labelling it the demonstrative. A replacement warrant is available from the same bytes (a fresh building image at 118:22 interpreted by the two 'this'-sayings that follow), but it has to pass the test that killed the original in the same edit. I also record the refs-mirror gap and one register violation. Credit where due: the signal that flags the stone's referent as an unsettled interpretive question the row holds rather than resolves is exactly the right handling.

challenges.claim: The row's stated driver -- three declarations opening with a 'this' demonstrative -- is false in both witnesses, and the demonstrative device it invokes actually straddles the row's own opening seam.
challenges.evidence: Of the 3 verses, only oshb:Ps.118.24 opens with the demonstrative (זֶה). oshb:Ps.118.22 opens אֶ֭בֶן ('stone'), with no demonstrative anywhere in the verse; oshb:Ps.118.23 opens with the prepositional phrase מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה and places its demonstrative זֹּ֑את fourth of 7 tokens. A skeleton sweep for a verse-initial demonstrative over Ps 118 returns exactly 2 verses -- 118:20 (זֶֽה) and 118:24 -- so the device crosses the 118:21|118:22 seam this row opens and is absent from 2 of the row's own 3 verses. The English does not rescue the claim: “The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” (web:Ps.118.22) has no demonstrative either, so even in WEB it is 2 of 3, not three.

challenges.claim: The observed_substrate_signals entry binds a Hebrew quote to a label the bytes do not support, calling a prepositional phrase a demonstrative.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads that vv23-24 open 'with a demonstrative' and supplies מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.118.23) as that demonstrative; those 2 tokens are the preposition-plus-name phrase rendered “This is Yahweh's doing.” (web:Ps.118.23) only because WEB fronts the clause's predicate. The verse's actual demonstrative is זֹּ֑את (oshb:Ps.118.23), token 4 of 7. Under the standing rule that a quote and its gloss cover the same span, this signal needs re-splicing, and observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the driver challenged above.

challenges.claim: Refs-mirror gap: five verses argued in prose outside the span are absent from boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.evidence: device_notes argues the row's position between vv19-21 and vv25-27; check_refs_mirror.py flags Ps.118.19, Ps.118.20, Ps.118.25, Ps.118.26, Ps.118.27 as argued_but_unmirrored (5 verses). Only Ps.118.21 of the neighbouring material is carried.

challenges.claim: Register violation: the rationale carries a positional row reference.
challenges.evidence: The rationale contrasts the unit with the shape of 'the preceding row'. The campaign register rule bans positional row references in row prose outright; cross-row contrasts are verse-anchored, e.g. 'the request-and-reply shape at 118:19-21'. The fix is a one-clause rewording that costs the argument nothing.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.118.25-Ps.118.27 holds: the hosanna plea, the blessing acclamation and the altar instruction form one festal scene, the 118:24|118:25 seam is a genuine shift from interpretive saying to direct plea, and the row is right to describe the antiphony without settling which party speaks. All 5 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and the psalm's identity numbering means no dual-cite is owed. The el-Yahweh count re-derived from pointed bytes rather than a skeleton sweep, since the short token is homographic: a byte-token match over all 29 verses returns exactly 1 verse, oshb:Ps.118.27, and the suffixed form at oshb:Ps.118.28 is correctly not counted. I extended the same byte-token match across psalms 115-118 (68 MT verses) and it still returns 1 verse, so the row's wider scope phrase holds as well. My challenge is confined to quote/gloss parity: two glosses render one token more than their quotes carry. Observation: pmarks_Ps.json records 1 paseq seg at MT Ps.118.27, sitting between the two tokens the row quotes as its el-Yahweh identification (seg layer, single-witness, not in the quotable verse bytes); the row makes no mark claim, so nothing is owed, but any future argument leaning on that juncture should cite the inventory.

challenges.claim: Both Hebrew quotes in the rationale stop short of the material their glosses render -- quote and gloss do not cover the same span.
challenges.evidence: The row quotes בָּר֣וּךְ הַ֭בָּא בְּשֵׁ֣ם (oshb:Ps.118.26) and glosses it “Blessed is he who comes in Yahweh's name!” (web:Ps.118.26); the divine name the gloss renders is the next token, so the byte-true run for that gloss is בָּר֣וּךְ הַ֭בָּא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.118.26). The same pattern recurs in the plea: the quote is אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה (oshb:Ps.118.25) while the gloss “Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh!” (web:Ps.118.25) renders through the following particle, i.e. אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה נָּ֑א (oshb:Ps.118.25). Both re-cuts collate at byte tier and neither changes the row's argument; truncating the Hebrew instead of re-cutting the gloss is the regression the quote/gloss parity rule names.

reviews.reasoning: The span is right and its central claim is a byte fact I re-derived by direct string equality rather than by trusting the row: oshb:Ps.118.1 and oshb:Ps.118.29 are byte-equal as whole verses at 7 whitespace tokens each, and verse-initial hodu falls at exactly those 2 verses in the psalm. All 6 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and the identity numbering means no dual-cite is owed. Confidence 'high' is earned for the frame. The defects are in the second signal, which makes two claims the bytes do not support: 118:28 does not repeat the phrase said to be doubled -- the verse's two God-addresses use different lexemes -- and the psalm's first-person-singular address to the deity is not confined to 118:28, since 118:21 carries the same thanksgiving verb with second-person suffix. Neither touches the span, and both are repairable inside the existing warrant. I also record a refs-mirror gap and a positional row reference.

challenges.claim: The 'doubled' claim is false at byte and consonantal tier: the phrase said to be repeated within 118:28 occurs once; the second address uses a different lexeme and no pronoun.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.118.28 is 5 whitespace tokens. The quoted phrase אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה (oshb:Ps.118.28) occurs exactly 1 time in the verse at byte tier and 1 time at skeleton tier (string counts over the verse bytes). The second address is 1 token, אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י (oshb:Ps.118.28), whose skeleton differs from that of אֵלִ֣י and which lacks the independent pronoun. WEB renders both colons “You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, I will exalt you.” (web:Ps.118.28), so the doubling is the translation's, not the substrate's -- and the row cites the Hebrew as the evidence.

challenges.claim: The exclusivity claim attached to this verse -- that it is the psalm's sole first-person-singular divine address -- is falsified by 118:21 (skeleton sweep of that verb form over Ps 118: 2 verses).
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.118.21 opens א֭וֹדְךָ -- first-person singular with a second-person suffix, addressed to the deity, rendered “I will give thanks to you, for you have answered me, and have become my salvation.” (web:Ps.118.21). A skeleton sweep of that form over Ps 118 returns 2 verses, 118:21 and 118:28 (the latter as וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ), so '1 of 29 verses' is the wrong count object for the claim as worded; 'sole' is defensible only if narrowed to the naming formula rather than to first-person-singular address.

The rejected_alternative argues against attaching the verse to vv25-27; check_refs_mirror.py flags Ps.118.25 and Ps.118.26 as argued_but_unmirrored (2 verses). Only web:Ps.118.27 of that span is carried in boundary_evidence_refs.

challenges.claim: Register violation: the rejected_alternative carries a positional row reference.
challenges.evidence: It reasons about 'the altar-procession row that precedes it'. Positional row references are banned in row prose; the verse anchor is already present in the same clause, so deleting the row reference is a lossless edit.
